records.finding: Section 3's constructive argument and Section 5.1's five-variable experiment give the passively trained learner active interventions and their observed consequences at evaluation. The manuscript correctly distinguishes learning an investigative strategy from resolving observational nonidentification without new information, and retains the finite environment/action-space transfer limitation.

The saved author version maps elicited relations to ancestral paths and adds a log-prior penalty in equations (3)-(7). The confidence analysis and error-tolerance experiments explicitly show that inaccurate priors can damage structural recovery. Both manuscript contexts retain the path-versus-adjacency distinction and avoid interpreting soft scores as calibrated causal probabilities.

The breadth-first construction visits each node once, while expansion prompts include accumulated graph information and cycle checks remove proposed edges. Section 4.3 and Table 4 report F1 .351 for the 221-node graph, omitted pairwise/GES configurations, a PC memory failure and the budget-based omission of the statistics-assisted variant. The manuscript distinguishes query count from total tokens/cost and treats acyclicity as insufficient to certify retained arrows.

The probability-to-prior mapping in Algorithm 2 depends on PC, exact search or DirectLiNGAM, with different edge/path semantics, forced/forbidden thresholds and an acyclic transformation for DirectLiNGAM. The experiments and failure discussion do not promise uniform gains. The manuscript preserves these conversions, source-specific failures and the distinction among response probabilities, bootstrap frequencies and scientific exclusions.

Sections 4-5 report stable repeated responses alongside conflicting quantitative priors, conventional imputation methods outperforming LLMs, ambiguous metadata/units and public-dataset recognition. The single manuscript context uses this as evidence about elicitation and benchmark design, not causal identification or a justification for inventing missing assignment mechanisms.

Figure 3 and the adjacent methodological taxonomy distinguish direct extraction, correction of statistical discoveries and prior integration. The manuscript cites the authors' own taxonomy only; its method-specific technical claims are supported by separately inspected original method papers rather than inheriting this survey's performance assertions.

The temporal graph setup assumes causal sufficiency, finite lag, an unrolled DAG and a known observational regime. Theorem 3.1 conditions population optimization on model capacity, intervention faithfulness, positive densities and finite entropy. The real data-center assessment explicitly lacks a true DAG and uses selected expert rules. Both manuscript contexts retain these restrictions and do not extend the result to arbitrary latent or irregularly observed bank processes.

Sections 3.4-3.5 bias CD-UCT's simulation policy using soft scores while retaining valid graph support; the MI-times-language prior is distinct from changing the numerical likelihood score. Figure 3 and Table 1 include cases where language-only priors do not improve results. The manuscript explicitly labels its additive score notation a project comparison device, preserves the method-specific mechanism and does not infer calibrated causal probabilities or uniform performance.
